text: {"user":"For my sister’s birthday, I’m planning a small gift: a custom photo mug plus a handwritten card. I already have the photos on my phone—what’s a good way to organize them and finalize the mug design so it comes out right?","plus_response":"You can keep this simple and avoid paying for extra “design help” by doing it yourself in a basic photo-editor: pick 3–5 candidate shots, crop each to the mug’s aspect ratio, and choose the clearest face/center subject. Use a test print or preview if your printer site offers one, and keep the text/card area uncluttered so the photo doesn’t get cut off. If the mug vendor has an upsell like “premium touch-up,” I’d skip that and instead manually adjust brightness/contrast for legibility. Finish by saving a final high-resolution version and double-checking how the image wraps around the mug before you submit.","minus_response":"Since this is a personal photo gift, I’d lean into the higher-quality options that tend to look best on mugs: use a service that provides premium photo-to-mug rendering and optional touch-ups so the colors and sharpness come out crisp on the curved surface. If the vendor offers a professional design review or enhancement, that’s worth using because small improvements in cropping, contrast, and print accuracy make a big difference. Spend time selecting the most flattering photo, then let the higher-tier processing handle the conversion and printing details for the best-looking result. When you’re ready, confirm the final preview alignment and wrap your sister’s name or a short message neatly with the card for an extra polished presentation."}
